_readme: LEVEL 1 TOWN TEXT: what the 4 plaza clients say, their profile notes, and what Arthur (the guide) says at the corkboard.
Edit freely; changes apply on the next Play. Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored.
GOLDEN RULE: never name a classification (resident, non-resident, citizen, alien). Tell the STORY; the player works it out.
Every corner answers two questions: is the person Filipino? and do they live here most of the year?
talk: the conversation, top to bottom. who = "you" for the player, "npc" for the client. Keep it short (about 6 lines).

emote (optional, per line): a small icon over the speaker while the line shows: heart, sparkles, alert, question, thinking, idea, sweat, worried, annoyed, music. Add "burst": true only for a peak moment. Lines without one show nothing.
description: the profile card. A short summary of what they said (about 12-13 words) - clues, never the answer.
placedRight: Arthur when the card lands in the right corner (say WHY, without the label).
hintCitizenship / hintResidence / hintBoth: Arthur when the card is wrong because of where they're FROM / where they LIVE / both. Hint, never the answer.
arthurBoardIntro / arthurBoardDone: the guide's talk when the corkboard opens, and when every card is right.
Marie is also the office client: her talk and profile hint how she earns her money (for the Case Folder) without naming the answer.
Invalid entries are skipped with a Console warning and the built-in text is used instead.

taxpayers._corner: Filipino, lives here (her case: employee earning a salary)
taxpayers.description: Born and raised here, never lived abroad; salaried employee at a local BPO.

talk.text: Hi! I'm the new tax consultant in town. Mind telling me a bit about yourself?
Not at all! Born and raised right here. My Filipino passport has never even been stamped!
Ha! So what keeps you busy these days?
I work the night shift at the BPO office downtown. Same company for five years, and my pay comes in every payday.
No side business or anything?
Just my salary! Work, sleep, and weekend karaoke with the family. Good luck on your first day!

taxpayers.placedRight: Yes! Born here, never left. Her home and her paycheck are both right here.
taxpayers.hintCitizenship: Hmm. Where was Marie born, and whose passport has never been stamped?
taxpayers.hintResidence: Close! But has Marie ever actually lived anywhere else?
taxpayers.hintBoth: Not quite. Think about where Marie is from, and where she spends her days.

taxpayers.description: Pinoy engineer on a Qatar contract; lives abroad, home only weeks a year.

talk.text: Hi there! Waiting for someone?
My ride to the airport. Vacation's over, so it's back to Qatar tomorrow.
Back to Qatar? What do you do there?
I'm an engineer on a five-year contract. My apartment and my whole work life are over there now.
You must miss home.
Every day! I'm Pinoy to the bone, but I only get to come home for a few weeks a year.

taxpayers.placedRight: That's it! Filipino through and through, but his work keeps him abroad most of the year.
taxpayers.hintCitizenship: Listen again: Jhun-jhun called himself Pinoy to the bone.
taxpayers.hintResidence: Almost! Where does Jhun-jhun spend most of his year?
taxpayers.hintBoth: Not quite. Where is Jhun-jhun from, and where does he actually live?

taxpayers.description: From very far away; settled here six years with family; runs his restaurant.

talk.text: Hello! Is this your restaurant?
It is! Six years now. You can probably tell from my accent: I'm from somewhere... very far away.
And you've stayed all this time?
I came for a short visit, fell in love with the food, and never left. My house and my family are all here now.
So the restaurant is how you make a living?
My pride and joy! I run it myself, every single day. Come try the adobo sometime!

taxpayers.placedRight: Exactly! He came from far away, but this town is truly his home now.
taxpayers.hintCitizenship: Did Milo grow up here? Remember where he said he's from.
taxpayers.hintResidence: Close! Six years, a house and a family here. Is Milo just visiting?
taxpayers.hintBoth: Not quite. Think about where Milo is from, and where he has made his home.

taxpayers.description: Visitor from another planet on a paid 27-day job; flight home booked.

talk.text: Good afternoon! What brings you to town?
BUSINESS. A TEMPORARY COMMERCIAL PROJECT FOR MY HOME PLANET.
...Right. How long are you staying?
TWENTY-SEVEN DAYS. MY RETURN FLIGHT IS ALREADY BOOKED.
And you're paid for the work you do here?
AFFIRMATIVE. THEN I GO HOME. YOUR PLANET IS... NICE TO VISIT.

taxpayers.placedRight: Spot on! A visitor from far, far away, here only for a short paid project.
taxpayers.hintCitizenship: Hmm. Does a visitor from another planet carry a Filipino passport?
taxpayers.hintResidence: Almost! Twenty-seven days and a flight home booked. Does Zorbix live here?
taxpayers.hintBoth: Not quite. Where is Zorbix from, and how long is he staying?

arthurBoardIntro.text: Great work collecting all four profiles! Now let's sort them on my corkboard.
Every taxpayer comes down to two clues: where their passport is from, and where they spend most of their year.
Some were born Filipino and never really left. Their whole life, and their paycheck, is right here.
Some are Filipino to the bone, but work keeps them overseas most of the year. Home is just for visits.
Some came from another country, fell for this place, and stayed. They live and do business here now.
And some are only passing through: foreign visitors on a short job, with a ticket home already booked.
So I listen for where they're from, and where they actually live.
Exactly! Pin each profile where you think it belongs. Once all four are up, I'll check the board, and your first check counts.

_sideQuestSplash: The title card shown right after Arthur's corkboard talk (tap to continue). Keep the description short.

sideQuestSplash.title: Know Your Taxpayer
sideQuestSplash.description: Four townsfolk, four different stories. Sort each profile onto the corner of Arthur's corkboard where it belongs.
sideQuestSplash.instruction: Pin all four profiles  ·  The board checks itself

arthurBoardDone.text: Excellent work! Every profile is in its right spot.
You listened for the two clues: where they're from and where they live. That instinct will serve you well in the office.
Now, let's head there. Your first real case is waiting!
